newsitem.title: CANADA: Virgin Atlantic to begin service to Canada.
newsitem.headline: Virgin Atlantic to begin service to Canada.

text.p: Virgin Group's Virgin Atlantic Airways expects to begin flights between Britian and Canada in the next year and is likely to order two Boeing Co 747s for the service, chairman Richard Branson said Monday.
"I think within the next 12 months we will be flying to Canada," Branson said in an interview. He said initial service would probably be offered between London's Heathrow airport and Toronto.
Branson was in Vancouver for the opening of his first Virgin Megastore music shop in Canada.

Branson said Virgin has several planes on order including three Boeing 747-400s, but the airline would need more planes to handle the Canadian traffic. "If we add Canada to the brew, we are going to need a couple more (planes). I suspect we would use 747s from Boeing in Seattle....We would need in a sense two planes to do the route," he said.

Branson said there were no plans to offer a low-cost domestic service in Canada akin to Virgin Express in Europe. Asked if Virgin would consider a link with struggling Canadian Airlines Corp, Branson said he was always open to talks, but Virgin was planning to go it alone.

Canadian is in an alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines. American is also proposing a trans-Atlantic alliance with British Airways Plc. Virgin and British Airways have been locked in a fierce rivalry and Branson has campaigned against the American alliance.

Branson said he was unaware of a report in Monday's Wall Street Journal that Jonathon Ornstein, chief executive of Virgin Express, was a top candidate for president and chief executive of Trans World Airlines Inc. Branson said he would be surprised if Ornstein took the job. Ornstein said earlier he had no intention of taking the TWA job.
